correctness.rationale: For G=complement H, Δ(H)=2 and n≥5 imply connected diameter≤2; the polar is the edge 1-Lipschitz polytope in the zero-sum subspace. Maximizing squared centered norm occurs at its TU-integral vertices, necessarily three levels 0,1,2. If a and b count extreme levels, every A×B edge must lie in H, forcing a,b≤2; squared norm is a+b−(b−a)²/n. The (1,2) case occurs per deleted degree-two vertex with value 3−1/n and the (2,2) case iff H has a C4 component with value 4; binary balanced cuts have norm Q_n/n. Norm comparison gives exact n=12 and n=16 cutoffs, equality at 16, plus tangent-facet counts by strictly convex polar maximizers. Independently enumerated all feasible ternary Lipschitz labelings for H=C_n,P_n,C4+isolates for n=5..8; max values and multiplicities equal theorem. This finite test is only a check; all-order proof uses TU and extremal levels.
